transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um... I guess I came in today because... well, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but some people have been pointing out a few things. It's probably nothing too serious, but they say they can actually see me, um, moving like I'm underwater? Like it takes me forever to just answer a simple question or get out of a chair. 

And then other times, I guess I've been pacing around my apartment a lot, just rubbing my hands together like I'm trying to shake off a really bad customer service call. I feel a little silly even bringing it up, honestly. Does that... does that make sense to come in for? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here.
Have you recently started taking any psychiatric medication?

Oh, um... no. No, I haven't. I'm not taking anything like that right now. I hope that's okay? I mean, I just take regular stuff like ibuprofen if I get a headache from staring at my screen at work, but nothing... nothing psychiatric. 

Is it bad that I haven't been taking anything? I really want to do whatever you think is best, doctor. I'm totally open to whatever you recommend, I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing here.
Have there been times when you were unable to move or speak, even though you wanted to?

Oh, no... no, nothing like that. I mean, even when I'm moving really slow like I mentioned earlier, I can always still move if I try. And I can definitely always talk. I kind of have to, you know, being on the phones all day for work. 

I hope that's a good thing? I'm really not trying to give you the wrong answer or anything, I just... I haven't ever felt totally frozen or unable to speak like that. Is it okay that I haven't experienced that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you ever had a distinct period when your mood was unusually elevated or irritable compared with your usual self?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I'm pretty even-keeled most of the time. I definitely wouldn't say I've ever been, like, unusually elevated or super irritable. I try really hard to be a positive person, especially with my job. You kind of have to be, right? 

I might get a little stressed sometimes if it's a really busy day, but I never take it out on anyone or get overly cranky. And I definitely don't get, like, hyper or anything. I hope that's the right answer? I just try to stay pretty steady, so I haven't really noticed anything like what you're describing. Does that sound normal to you?
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I feel depressed most of the day. I mean, everyone gets a little down sometimes, right? Like if work is stressful or I get a really tough customer on the line, but... I try really hard to just brush it off and stay upbeat. I definitely wouldn't say it's every day or anything severe like that. 

I really try to keep a good attitude. I hope that's okay? I just don't want you to think I'm, like, wallowing or not trying my best to stay positive. It's normal to just have a regular bad day here and there, isn't it?
Have you heard voices when no one else was present?

Um... well, I mean, I don't know if I'd call it "voices" exactly. That sounds a little intense, right? It's probably just stress from the job, honestly. 

Sometimes, like... if my laptop is closed and I'm totally off the clock, no phones ringing or anything... I'll hear, like, the little beep from my old headset. Or I'll hear someone—like a supervisor, maybe?—just say my name, or say "too slow." 

But it's just a work thing! Like when you hear your alarm clock even when it's not going off. It's not a big deal, I promise. It just means I'm really dedicated to my job, right? I hope that doesn't sound crazy or anything. Is that pretty common for people who do a lot of phone work?
How long have you been hearing these beeps or someone saying your name or “too slow” when no one is present?

Um... well, it's been a little while, I guess. Maybe... a year and eight months? Give or take? But I really don't want you to think it's because I'm depressed or anything like that! 

Even when I'm feeling totally fine and trying my best to stay positive, I still hear the beeps or the "too slow" stuff. And, um, I guess I also sometimes feel like... like they're tracking my calls or monitoring me even when I'm not working. But again, that's just because I want to do a good job, you know? It's not just when I'm feeling down. I just want to make sure I'm meeting all my metrics. 

I hope that doesn't sound too weird? I mean, a year and a half isn't that long in the grand scheme of things, right? I'm sure lots of people take their work home with them like that.
Have these experiences caused your work performance to worsen compared with how you worked before?

Um... well, I mean, I can still pay my rent and keep a roof over my head, so it's not like I'm totally failing or anything! I really try to keep things together. 

But, I guess... maybe I've lost a little bit of momentum? Like, sometimes I might miss a deadline, or... I guess I'll avoid taking some calls if I feel like they're monitoring me too closely. And I know that probably makes me look a little unreliable to my supervisors, which I hate, because I really do want to be a good employee! I just... I get a little overwhelmed. 

And, um, I guess outside of work, I don't see my friends as much as I used to. And sometimes little things, like running errands or making meals... or even just going hiking, which I used to love... they kind of slide a bit. Unless I really force myself to do them. 

But I'm still managing okay, right? I mean, everyone gets a little behind on chores or work sometimes. I just hope I'm not coming across as lazy or anything. I really am trying my best to stay on top of things!
Have people ever told you that your speech is difficult to follow because your thoughts jump from one topic to another?

Um... no, no one's ever really said anything like that to me. I try really hard to make sure I'm communicating clearly, especially because of my job. You have to be super clear on the phone, you know? 

I mean, maybe sometimes if I'm a little flustered, I might talk a little fast, or... or try to get all my points across at once so I don't forget them? But I always make sure people understand what I'm saying. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm confusing or hard to talk to. I'm pretty good at staying on track, I promise. That's a good thing, right?
Besides the belief that your work calls are being monitored, have you had any other unusual beliefs that other people do not share?

Um... well... I really don't want you to think I'm paranoid or anything like that. I know it might sound a little strange at first. But, um... even when I'm having a pretty okay week, like when I'm feeling fine and trying to be positive, I still get... well, I get convinced that the ticketing software from my old job is somehow tracking me. Like it's following me through different job sites online and secretly flagging me as unreliable to anyone who might look at my profile. 

But honestly, with how much data companies collect and share nowadays, it's not that unusual to worry about your digital footprint, right? I mean, I just really care about my career and I don't want any bad metrics following me around. I just want to make sure I'm always seen as a good worker. I hope that makes sense? I definitely don't want to come across as crazy or anything, I just want to protect my reputation.
Have there been any periods lasting a month or longer when you had neither the voices nor the belief that you were being monitored or tracked?

Um... a whole month without them? I... well, I really wish I could say yes, because I try so hard to just focus on my work and be positive. But... honestly? No, probably not a full month. 

I guess... I mean, I don't want it to sound worse than it is, but the tracking worries and, um, the voices... they've actually been around for about a year and eight months now. But I mostly just keep it to myself! And, um... they don't just happen when I'm going through a really bad slump, either. Even when I'm not feeling super sad, and I'm having a pretty good, productive week... they're still kind of there in the background. 

But I don't let it ruin everything, I promise! I still show up and do what I need to do. I hope that doesn't make my situation sound too severe? I really am trying my best to just push through it and be a good employee. I'm doing okay considering, right?
Before these experiences began, had you been using any recreational drugs or misusing prescription medications?

Oh, no, no. Definitely not. I... I know sometimes people might do that sort of thing to cope, and I don't judge anyone, but I've always stayed completely away from recreational drugs. And I'd never misuse a prescription, either. 

I just... I really value being responsible, especially with my job. I wouldn't want to do anything that could mess up my performance or get me in trouble, you know? I always just try to follow the rules and do exactly what I'm supposed to do. I like to keep a clear head so I can be reliable. That's a good thing, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything right on my end.
